items.title: Trump reportedly challenges European leaders over further Ukraine aid
items.summary: During a call from Air Force One after meeting Putin and Xi, President Donald Trump reportedly questioned European plans for further military and financial support to Ukraine, including a proposed €70 billion package. Accounts attributed to participants say he urged greater emphasis on peace negotiations and described Putin as willing to negotiate.

items.title: Merz raises possibility of easing Russian sanctions as peace talks progress
items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said sanctions against Russia could potentially be lifted as negotiations toward resolving the Ukraine conflict advance, according to a Russian news agency report. No specific sanctions relief or timetable was announced.

items.title: Ukraine reportedly seeks more than $358 million in UN winter humanitarian funding
items.summary: A report says Ukraine has requested more than $358 million from the United Nations for winter humanitarian operations, about $80 million above the previous year's amount. It describes planned spending on repairs to communal infrastructure, refugee cash assistance and evacuations from frontline areas.

items.title: Dutch and Austrian embassies reportedly damaged during Kyiv air attack
items.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha said the Dutch and Austrian embassies in Kyiv sustained damage during the day's strikes. The Dutch foreign minister described minor damage after a projectile landed behind the embassy, said no staff were injured and indicated authorities were investigating the cause.

items.title: Russian embassy seeks Dutch explanation over alleged Destinus role in strikes
items.summary: Russia's embassy in the Netherlands requested clarification from Dutch authorities following an NRC investigation alleging that at least 40 employees of defence manufacturer Destinus may have travelled to Ukraine and participated in drone launches toward Russia. The embassy said those involved in attacks causing civilian casualties should bear responsibility; the allegations are not court findings.
